type OrderInput struct {
	OrderID string `json:"order_id"`
}

type OrderStatus struct {
	OrderID string `json:"order_id"`
	Status  string `json:"status"`
}

func newOrderTool() *gent.ToolFunc[OrderInput, OrderStatus] {
	return gent.NewToolFunc(
		"lookup_order",
		"Get the current status of an order by its ID.",
		schema.Object(map[string]*schema.Property{
			"order_id": schema.String("The order ID, for example order-1001."),
		}, "order_id"),
		func(ctx context.Context, input OrderInput) (OrderStatus, error) {
			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
				return OrderStatus{}, err
			}
			// Use a fixed record so this example needs no database. Replace it with your API.
			if input.OrderID != "order-1001" {
				return OrderStatus{}, fmt.Errorf("order not found: %s", input.OrderID)
			}
			return OrderStatus{OrderID: input.OrderID, Status: "shipped"}, nil
		},
	)
}

// Build the tool registry once, before you use the runner for questions.
func newRunner(model gent.Model) *executor.Runner {
	chain := toolchain.New()
	chain.RegisterTool(newOrderTool())

	term := termination.NewText("answer").WithGuidance(
		"Give a short answer with the order ID and its status.",
	)
	loop := react.NewAgent(model).
		WithToolChain(chain).
		WithTermination(term).
		WithBehaviorAndContext("Help the user check an order.").
		WithCriticalRules("Use lookup_order for order facts. Do not invent a status.")

	return executor.NewRunner(loop, executor.DefaultConfig())
}

func ask(ctx context.Context, runner *executor.Runner, question string) (string, error) {
	// Each question gets its own history, counters, and cancellation state.
	data := gent.NewBasicLoopData(&gent.Task{Text: question})
	execCtx := gent.NewExecutionContext(ctx, "order-helper", data)
	limits := gent.DefaultLimits()
	for i := range limits {
		if limits[i].Key == gent.SCIterations.Self() {
			limits[i].MaxValue = 6
		}
	}
	execCtx.SetLimits(limits)

func run() error {
	key, modelName := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"), os.Getenv("GENT_MODEL")
	if key == "" || modelName == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("set OPENAI_API_KEY and GENT_MODEL first")
	}
	model := models.NewOpenAI(key, modelName)
	runner := newRunner(model)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	answer, err := ask(ctx, runner, "What is the status of order-1001?")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println(answer)
	return nil
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"time"

	"github.com/rickchristie/gent"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/agents/react"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/executor"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/models"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/schema"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/termination"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/toolchain"
)

type OrderInput struct {
	OrderID string `json:"order_id"`
}

type OrderStatus struct {
	OrderID string `json:"order_id"`
	Status  string `json:"status"`
}

func newOrderTool() *gent.ToolFunc[OrderInput, OrderStatus] {
	return gent.NewToolFunc(
		"lookup_order",
		"Get the current status of an order by its ID.",
		schema.Object(map[string]*schema.Property{
			"order_id": schema.String("The order ID, for example order-1001."),
		}, "order_id"),
		func(ctx context.Context, input OrderInput) (OrderStatus, error) {
			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
				return OrderStatus{}, err
			}
			// Use a fixed record so this example needs no database. Replace it with your API.
			if input.OrderID != "order-1001" {
				return OrderStatus{}, fmt.Errorf("order not found: %s", input.OrderID)
			}
			return OrderStatus{OrderID: input.OrderID, Status: "shipped"}, nil
		},
	)
}

// Build the tool registry once, before you use the runner for questions.
func newRunner(model gent.Model) *executor.Runner {
	chain := toolchain.New()
	chain.RegisterTool(newOrderTool())

	term := termination.NewText("answer").WithGuidance(
		"Give a short answer with the order ID and its status.",
	)
	loop := react.NewAgent(model).
		WithToolChain(chain).
		WithTermination(term).
		WithBehaviorAndContext("Help the user check an order.").
		WithCriticalRules("Use lookup_order for order facts. Do not invent a status.")

	return executor.NewRunner(loop, executor.DefaultConfig())
}

func ask(ctx context.Context, runner *executor.Runner, question string) (string, error) {
	// Each question gets its own history, counters, and cancellation state.
	data := gent.NewBasicLoopData(&gent.Task{Text: question})
	execCtx := gent.NewExecutionContext(ctx, "order-helper", data)
	limits := gent.DefaultLimits()
	for i := range limits {
		if limits[i].Key == gent.SCIterations.Self() {
			limits[i].MaxValue = 6
		}
	}
	execCtx.SetLimits(limits)

	result, err := runner.Execute(execCtx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if result.TerminationReason != gent.TerminationSuccess {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("run ended with %s", result.TerminationReason)
	}
	if len(result.Output) != 1 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("expected one text answer, got %d parts", len(result.Output))
	}
	answer, ok := result.Output[0].(gent.TextContent)
	if !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("expected text, got %T", result.Output[0])
	}
	return answer.Text, nil
}

func run() error {
	key, modelName := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"), os.Getenv("GENT_MODEL")
	if key == "" || modelName == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("set OPENAI_API_KEY and GENT_MODEL first")
	}
	model := models.NewOpenAI(key, modelName)
	runner := newRunner(model)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	answer, err := ask(ctx, runner, "What is the status of order-1001?")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println(answer)
	return nil
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

type OrderInput struct {
	OrderID string `json:"order_id"`
}

func newAgent(model gent.Model) *react.Agent {
	tool := gent.NewToolFunc("lookup_order", "Read an order status.",
		schema.Object(map[string]*schema.Property{
			"order_id": schema.String("The order ID, such as order-1001."),
		}, "order_id"), func(ctx context.Context, input OrderInput) (string, error) {
			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
			if input.OrderID != "order-1001" {
				return "", fmt.Errorf("order not found: %s", input.OrderID)
			}
			return "Order order-1001 has shipped.", nil
		})
	return react.NewAgent(model).RegisterTool(tool).
		WithRecoveryVersion("order-streaming/v1").
		WithBehaviorAndContext("Help the user check an order.").
		WithCriticalRules("Use lookup_order for order facts. Do not invent a status.").
		WithCallOptions(gent.WithMaxTokens(1024))
}

02 / GO + DATABASE STEP 02


Implement gent.Recorder.Save.



Gent passes a SaveBatch at each acceptance boundary, including streamed progress. A batch can
contain events, history changes, runtime counters, and a checkpoint.



WHAT TO CODE


Add store.go. Put this method on Writer. Commit all state in one database transaction and return nil
only after the transaction succeeds.








server/store.go


GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


// Save is the Gent persistence boundary. Returning nil means the transaction has committed.
func (w *Writer) Save(ctx context.Context, batch *gent.SaveBatch) error {
	if batch.RunId != w.runID {
		return gent.ErrWrongRun
	}
	return w.store.db.Update(func(tx *bolt.Tx) error {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		bucket := tx.Bucket([]byte(w.runID))
		if bucket == nil || binary.BigEndian.Uint64(bucket.Get([]byte("owner"))) != w.fence {
			return errStaleWriter
		}
		view, err := w.store.read(bucket, w.runID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		// ApplyBatch checks the previous cursor, event order, digest, and duplicate batch IDs.
		next, err := gent.ApplyBatch(view, batch, w.store.codecs)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("apply saved batch: %w", err)
		}
		data, err := w.store.codecs.Marshal(next)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return bucket.Put([]byte("view"), data)
	})
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Database choice

    
bbolt is a real file database with atomic transactions. This short-run example rewrites one full
RunView; a larger store should keep append-only batches and maintain its view in the same
transaction.

    2. 

  2. 
Writer fence

    
The transaction rejects a worker whose owner number is old. Canceling a context alone cannot prevent
an old worker from saving.

    3. 

  3. 
gent.ApplyBatch

    
Checks the previous cursor, consecutive event numbers, batch digest, and duplicate identity. An
identical retry is safe.

    4. 

  4. 
CodecRegistry.Marshal / Unmarshal

    
Keep concrete Go content and metadata types. Ordinary JSON decoding of a RunView is not a
restoration format.









RESULT


A saved view and its cursor always describe the same committed data.

02 / GO + DATABASE STEP 04

GET /api/runs/{id}/state loads one committed RunView, rebuilds the trace, and returns the subset
needed by this React client. It also works after a restart.

func (a *API) snapshot(runID string) (BrowserState, error) {
	saved, err := a.store.load(runID)
	if err != nil {
		return BrowserState{}, err
	}
	seq, err := trace.RestoreSequencer(saved, displayConfig(a.store.codecs))
	if err != nil {
		return BrowserState{}, err
	}
	defer seq.Close()
	return browserState(seq.Snapshot()), nil
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Display versus recovery

    
BrowserState holds previews, accepted answers, and status. The database keeps the full RunView,
including recovery data.

    2. 

  2. 
trace.RestoreSequencer

    
Rebuilds display state from saved activity. It does not resume the agent or call a model.

    3. 

  3. 
Snapshot.LastEventNumber

    
The cursor used for this browser view. view.go sends it as a decimal string so JavaScript can
compare it with BigInt.









RESULT


The frontend can replace its display state with one consistent response.

	defer func() {

			log.Printf("close WebSocket: %v", err)

	if err := conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(20 * time.Second)); err != nil {

	}
	conn.SetPongHandler(func(string) error {
		return conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(20 * time.Second))
	})
	closed := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(closed)
		for {
			if _, _, err := conn.ReadMessage(); err != nil {
				log.Printf("WebSocket reader stopped: %v", err)
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	if err := socketWrite(conn, Frame{Kind: "ready", RunID: id}); err != nil {
		log.Printf("write ready: %v", err)
		return
	}

Line by line


  1. 
SubscribeWithConfig

    
Use a bounded queue. OverflowCloseSubscriber closes a slow subscription instead of blocking the
agent or silently losing events.

    2. 

  2. 
Connection ownership

    
One goroutine reads control messages and one writes data. Deadlines, ping/pong, unsubscribe, and
Close release socket resources.

    3. 

  3. 
ready

    
The client starts buffering as soon as it receives events. It fetches the snapshot only after it
receives ready for the correct run ID.









RESULT


Every event after ready is covered by the subscription or a later full reload.

A client must see every cursor position, even when an event has no visible text. Do not filter the
stream down to token events and then require contiguous numbers.

subscription, request a fresh subscription and snapshot.

	tick := time.NewTicker(5 * time.Second)
	defer tick.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-a.worker.Done():
			return
		case <-closed:
			return
		case event, ok := <-updates:
			if !ok {
				if err := socketWrite(conn, Frame{Kind: "resync", RunID: id}); err != nil {
					log.Printf("write resync: %v", err)
				}
				return
			}
			if err := socketWrite(conn, eventFrame(event)); err != nil {
				log.Printf("write event: %v", err)
				return
			}
		case <-tick.C:
			// A worker can start after an idle client joins. Reconnect to the new sequencer.
			if a.active(id) != live {
				return
			}
			if err := conn.WriteControl(websocket.PingMessage, nil,
				time.Now().Add(5*time.Second)); err != nil {
				log.Printf("write ping: %v", err)
				return
			}
			if err := socketWrite(conn, Frame{Kind: "heartbeat", RunID: id}); err != nil {
				log.Printf("write heartbeat: %v", err)
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

Worker changes

    
An idle subscriber reconnects when a new worker starts. A finished worker releases its sequencer and
leaves the database view intact.

func (a *API) routes(uiPath string) http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/runs", a.createRun)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/runs/{id}/state", a.getState)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/runs/{id}/events", a.streamEvents)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/runs/{id}/resume", a.resumeRun)
	mux.Handle("/", http.FileServer(http.Dir(uiPath)))
	return mux
}

package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/rickchristie/gent"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/models"
)

func env(name, fallback string) string {
	if value := os.Getenv(name); value != "" {
		return value
	}
	return fallback
}

func serve() error {
	worker, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	factory := func() gent.Model { return &DemoModel{Delay: 600 * time.Millisecond} }
	if key := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		name := os.Getenv("GENT_MODEL")
		if name == "" {
			return errors.New("set GENT_MODEL when using OPENAI_API_KEY")
		}
		factory = func() gent.Model { return models.NewOpenAI(key, name) }
	}
	codecs := gent.NewCodecRegistry()
	if err := newAgent(factory()).RegisterCodecs(codecs); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	store, err := openStore(env("RUN_DB", "runs.db"), codecs)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() {
		if err := store.db.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Printf("close database: %v", err)
		}
	}()
	api := &API{store: store, model: factory, worker: worker, running: map[string]*liveRun{}}
	listener, err := net.Listen("tcp", env("API_ADDR", "127.0.0.1:8080"))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	server := &http.Server{Handler: api.routes(env("UI_DIR", "../client/dist")),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}
	shutdown := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(shutdown)
		<-worker.Done()
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		if err := server.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
			log.Printf("HTTP shutdown: %v", err)
		}
	}()
	log.Printf("LISTEN http://%s", listener.Addr().String())
	err = server.Serve(listener)
	stop()
	<-shutdown
	api.wait.Wait()
	if errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
		return nil
	}
	return err
}

func main() {
	if err := serve(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

    3.

export class Gap extends Error {}

// Gent uses uint64. Decimal strings on the wire and BigInt here keep every cursor exact.
export function cursor(value: string): bigint {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || !/^(0|[1-9]\d*)$/.test(value)) {
    throw new Error("Invalid event cursor");
  }
  return BigInt(value);
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Name a missing event

    
The reducer throws Gap when the next event number is missing. Reload the saved state.

    2. 

  2. 
Validate the wire value

    
Accept a canonical non-negative decimal string before converting it to an integer.

    3. 

  3. 
Compare without rounding

    
BigInt preserves every uint64 event number, including values above 2^53.

    4. 

  4. 
Checkpoint.EventNumber

    
This can be older than the saved progress cursor. It tells the worker where to continue, not the
browser where to deduplicate.

    5. 

  5. 
HistoryRevision / draft Revision

    
These identify history changes or local edits. They are not the cursor for the complete event feed.

    6. 

  6. 
Run ID + cursor

    
Reject another run's snapshot or event. Compare cursors only within the same run.









RESULT


The browser can compare exact event numbers, including values above 2^53.

missing, request a fresh subscription and complete snapshot.

export function applyEvent(state: State, frame: Frame): State {
  if (frame.runId !== state.runId || frame.event?.runId !== state.runId) {
    throw new Error("Wrong run");
  }
  const number = cursor(frame.eventNumber!);
  const previous = cursor(state.lastEventNumber);
  if (number <= previous) return state;
  if (number !== previous + 1n) throw new Gap("Missing event: reload the saved state");
  const event = frame.event!;
  const payload = event.payload ?? {};
  const next = { ...state, lastEventNumber: frame.eventNumber! };
  if (event.type === "execution_started") next.status = "running";
  if (event.type === "execution_finished") next.status = payload.status!;
  if (event.type === "limit_exceeded") next.status = "limit_exceeded";
  if (event.type === "model_call_started") {
    next.previews = [
      ...state.previews,
      {
        id: event.modelCallId!,
        attemptId: event.attemptId!,
        contextId: event.contextId!,
        status: "running",
        parts: [],
      },
    ];
  }
  if (event.type === "model_stream_chunk" || event.type === "model_call_finished") {
    next.previews = state.previews.map((preview) => {
      if (preview.id !== event.modelCallId || preview.attemptId !== event.attemptId) return preview;
      if (event.type === "model_call_finished") {
        return { ...preview, status: event.error ? "failed" : "succeeded" };
      }
      return { ...preview, parts: appendParts(preview.parts, payload.metaContent ?? []) };
    });
  }
  if (event.type === "attempt_started" || event.type === "attempt_interrupted") {
    next.previews = state.previews.map((preview) => {
      const old =
        event.type === "attempt_started"
          ? preview.attemptId !== event.attemptId
          : preview.attemptId === event.attemptId;
      const sameContext = preview.contextId === event.contextId;
      return old && sameContext && preview.status === "running"
        ? { ...preview, status: "interrupted" }
        : preview;
    });
  }
  if (event.type === "execution_content") {
    const answer: Answer = {
      contextId: event.contextId!,
      messageId: payload.messageId!,
      sourceMessageIds: payload.sourceMessageIds ?? [],
      text: payload.content ?? "",
    };
    const exists = state.answers.some((item) => item.contextId === answer.contextId);
    next.answers = exists
      ? state.answers.map((item) => (item.contextId === answer.contextId ? answer : item))
      : [...state.answers, answer];
  }
  // Even events without a visible change must advance the canonical cursor.
  return next;
}

export function catchUp(snapshot: State, buffered: Frame[]): State {
  let next = snapshot;
  for (const frame of buffered) next = applyEvent(next, frame);
  return next;
}

Line by line


  1. 
number ≤ previous

    
Duplicate delivery is normal after a snapshot overlaps with a socket buffer. Ignore it without
changing text or counters.

    2. 

  2. 
number = previous + 1

    
Apply the change and advance the cursor together. Unknown display event types still advance the
cursor.

    3. 

  3. 
Attempt identity

    
Keep retries separate with ModelCallId plus AttemptId. This uses one root context; child context
trees need a matching reducer.

    4. 

  4. 
execution_content

    
Replace the accepted answer with Content. Do not append it to the preview. SourceMessageIds identify
the previews it replaces.









RESULT


Duplicate events cannot duplicate text. A gap triggers a fresh state read.

    socket.onmessage = (message) => {
      if (!valid()) return;
      try {
        const frame: Frame = JSON.parse(String(message.data));
        if (frame.runId !== runId) throw new Error("Wrong socket run");
        watchConnection();
        if (frame.kind === "ready") {
          ready = true;
          void refresh();
          return;
        }
        if (frame.kind === "resync") {
          reconnect("server requested a fresh subscription");
          return;
        }
        if (frame.kind === "heartbeat") return;
        if (frame.kind !== "event") throw new Error("Unknown frame kind");
        if (!state || loading) {
          buffer.push(frame);
          bufferBytes += String(message.data).length * 2;
          if (buffer.length > 1024 || bufferBytes > 2 * 1024 * 1024) {
            reconnect("snapshot buffer is full");
          }
          return;
        }
        state = applyEvent(state, frame);
        publish(state);
        if (terminal(state)) void refresh();
      } catch (error) {
        reconnect(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
      }
    };

Line by line

ready before fetch

    
WebSocket open alone is not sufficient. The ready message confirms the server has installed the
accepted-event subscription.

    2. 

  2. 
While loading

    
Continue adding events to the queue. Never pause the socket listener while awaiting fetch.

    3. 

  3. 
Bounded buffering

    
At 1,024 events or 2 MiB, reconnect and load a fresh snapshot. The new snapshot covers the discarded
accepted events.









RESULT


Events have one ordered path before, during, and after the snapshot request.







03 / REACT + TYPESCRIPT STEP 04


Replace state, skip duplicates, drain the buffer.



Suppose the buffer contains events 80, 81, and 82. A complete snapshot through 81 already includes
80 and 81. Apply only 82, then accept 83 from the live socket.



WHAT TO CODE


Add refresh() inside connect(). After fetch returns, catchUp installs the snapshot and applies all
later buffered events in the same JavaScript task.








client/src/connection.ts


TYPESCRIPT
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


    async function refresh() {
      if (!valid() || !ready || loading) return;
      loading = true;
      controller = new AbortController();
      fetchTimer = setTimeout(() => controller?.abort(), 10000);
      status("Loading saved state");
      try {
        const snapshot = await transport.load(runId, controller.signal);
        if (!valid()) return;
        if (snapshot.runId !== runId) throw new Error("Wrong snapshot run");
        if (state && cursor(snapshot.lastEventNumber) < cursor(state.lastEventNumber)) {
          throw new Error("Snapshot cursor moved backwards");
        }
        state = catchUp(snapshot, buffer);
        buffer = [];
        bufferBytes = 0;
        loading = false;
        attempt = 0;
        publish(state);
        // Only a full saved snapshot proves that the entire terminal batch is present.
        if (terminal(snapshot)) {
          stopped = true;
          closeCurrent();
          status("Complete");
          return;
        }
        status("Live");
        clearTimeout(poll);
        poll = setTimeout(() => void refresh(), transport.pollMs);
      } catch (error) {
        reconnect(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
      } finally {
        clearTimeout(fetchTimer);
      }
    }




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
One in-flight state read

    
The loading flag prevents overlapping fetches. Generation checks reject responses from a replaced
connection.

    2. 

  2. 
Install the snapshot and drain the buffer

    
Skip events covered by the snapshot. Apply the later events in order before going live.

    3. 

  3. 
Full terminal snapshot

    
A terminal display event can precede other events in its batch. Stop only after a full saved
snapshot confirms completion.

    4. 

  4. 
Periodic refresh

    
Reload every five seconds, even when no gap is visible. This finds a lost final update that has no
later event to reveal the gap.









RESULT


The page reaches the same view as the server without applying any event twice.







03 / REACT + TYPESCRIPT STEP 05


Own the connection in an Effect.



The connection belongs to the selected run. Changing the run or unmounting the component must close
the socket, abort fetches, and clear retry and poll timers.

TYPESCRIPT

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { connectRun } from "./connection";
import type { State } from "./state";

export function useRun(runId: string) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<State | null>(null);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState("Choose a run");
  useEffect(() => {
    setState(null);
    if (!runId) return;
    let frame = 0;
    let latest: State;
    const stop = connectRun(
      runId,
      (next) => {
        latest = next;
        // Apply every event, but render at most once per browser frame.
        if (!frame)
          frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
            frame = 0;
            setState(latest);
          });
      },
      setStatus,
    );
    return () => {
      stop();
      cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    };
  }, [runId]);
  return { state, status };
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Cleanup

    
connectRun returns a stop function. It closes the socket, aborts pending reads, clears timers, and
rejects stale callbacks.

    2. 

  2. 
[runId]

    
Create a new connection when the selected run changes. React StrictMode can run setup and cleanup
twice during development.









RESULT


The UI can switch runs, unmount, and refresh without leaving old listeners.

import { StrictMode, useState } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { useRun } from "./useRun";
import "./style.css";

function App() {
  const [runId, setRunId] = useState(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("run") ?? "");
  const [error, setError] = useState("");
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const { state, status } = useRun(runId);

  async function post(resume: boolean) {
    setBusy(true);
    setError("");
    try {
      const response = await fetch(
        resume ? `/api/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}/resume` : "/api/runs",
        {
          method: "POST",
          headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
          body: JSON.stringify({ question: "What is the status of order-1001?" }),
        },
      );
      const body = await response.json();
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(body.error);
      const url = new URL(location.href);
      url.searchParams.set("run", body.runId);
      history.replaceState(null, "", url);
      // A resumed run uses the same ID. Reload to start the same catch-up protocol again.
      if (resume) location.reload();
      else setRunId(body.runId);
    } catch (error) {
      setError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <p className="eyebrow">GENT / STREAMING EXAMPLE</p>
      <h1>An answer you can refresh.</h1>
      <p>Start a run, then refresh this page while the preview arrives.</p>
      <div className="actions">
        <button disabled={busy} onClick={() => void post(false)}>
          Start order lookup
        </button>
        <button disabled={busy || !runId} onClick={() => void post(true)}>
          Resume saved run
        </button>
      </div>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
      <p role="status">{status}</p>
      {state && (
        <>
          <p>
            Run <code>{runId}</code> · Event <code>{state.lastEventNumber}</code>
          </p>
          <p>Run status: {state.status}</p>
          {state.previews.map((preview) => {
            const replaced = new Set(
              state.answers
                .filter((answer) => answer.contextId === preview.contextId)
                .flatMap((answer) => answer.sourceMessageIds ?? []),
            );
            const parts = preview.parts.filter((part) => !replaced.has(part.messageId));
            if (!parts.length) return null;
            return (
              <section key={`${preview.id}/${preview.attemptId}`} aria-label="Model preview">
                <h2>Preview · {preview.status}</h2>
                {parts.map((part, index) => (
                  <p key={index}>
                    <small>{part.type}</small>
                    <br />
                    {part.text}
                  </p>
                ))}
              </section>
            );
          })}
          {state.answers.map((answer) => (
            <section key={answer.contextId} aria-label="Accepted answer">
              <h2>Accepted answer</h2>
              <p>{answer.text || "(empty answer)"}</p>
            </section>
          ))}
        </>
      )}
    </main>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App />
  </StrictMode>,
);





READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Remember the run in the URL

    
A refresh reads the same run ID and starts the subscribe-buffer-snapshot protocol.

    2. 

  2. 
Keep the page shareable

    
Update the URL after creation. A resumed run keeps the same ID.

    3. 

  3. 
Custom model adapters

    
Set CandidateSource.MessageIds to the same local IDs used by the candidate's preview chunks.
Gent scopes those IDs per call.

    4. 

  4. 
Hide only the replaced preview

    
Keep unrelated metadata. Remove the parts named by the accepted answer's source IDs.

    5. 

  5. 
Accepted text

    
The final answer can differ from the preview, including formatting or an empty accepted answer.
Replace it as a complete value.









The HTML guide works offline. Building the examples requires Go or Node.js
and their dependencies. Scenario 2 includes a local model that needs no API credentials.






04 / FRESH WORKER STEP 01


Read the saved RunView from scenario 2.



A browser refresh and a worker restart are different operations. The browser rebuilds display state.
A replacement worker needs the full saved RunView.



WHAT TO CODE


Create fresh model and agent objects. Register the agent's codecs before loading the database
bytes. Call Store.load with the existing run ID.








server/store.go


GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


func (s *Store) read(bucket *bolt.Bucket, runID string) (gent.RunView, error) {
	view := gent.RunView{SchemaVersion: gent.RunSchemaVersion, RunId: runID}
	data := bucket.Get([]byte("view"))
	if data == nil {
		return view, nil
	}
	err := s.codecs.Unmarshal(data, &view)
	return view, err
}

func (s *Store) load(runID string) (gent.RunView, error) {
	var view gent.RunView
	err := s.db.View(func(tx *bolt.Tx) error {
		bucket := tx.Bucket([]byte(runID))
		if bucket == nil {
			return errMissing
		}
		var err error
		view, err = s.read(bucket, runID)
		return err
	})
	return view, err
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
RegisterCodecs before decode

    
newAgent(model).RegisterCodecs(codecs) registers the tool and agent state types. Use that registry
in openStore.

    2. 

  2. 
Keep progress beyond the checkpoint

    
Do not trim Activity to Checkpoint.EventNumber. Saved model output and accounting may be newer.









RESULT


You have the complete accepted run, including its continuation checkpoint.







04 / FRESH WORKER STEP 02


Fence the old worker before continuing.



The previous worker can still be saving after its context is canceled. A new owner number makes its
next database write fail inside the save transaction.



WHAT TO CODE


Call Store.claim for the existing run ID. Pass the returned Writer to the restored context. The Save
method from scenario 2 checks this number on every transaction.








server/store.go


GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


// A new owner fences earlier workers. The check and state write use the same transaction.
func (s *Store) claim(runID string) (*Writer, error) {
	w := &Writer{store: s, runID: runID}
	err := s.db.Update(func(tx *bolt.Tx) error {
		bucket, err := tx.CreateBucketIfNotExists([]byte(runID))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		w.fence, err = bucket.NextSequence()
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return bucket.Put([]byte("owner"), binary.BigEndian.AppendUint64(nil, w.fence))
	})
	return w, err
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Same transaction

    
Checking the fence separately from the data write leaves a race. bbolt checks the owner and writes
the complete view in one update.

    2. 

  2. 
Give the new owner a higher number

    
The Save transaction checks this value. An older worker cannot advance the run.

    3. 

  3. 
Multiple processes

    
bbolt locks its database file to one process. A shared SQL store needs an equivalent transactional
lease or fencing check.









RESULT


The replacement worker is the only writer allowed to advance this run.







04 / FRESH WORKER STEP 03


Do not blindly repeat an external write.



A process can stop after a tool changes an external system but before its result is saved. A
tool-ready checkpoint alone cannot prove whether the tool completed.



WHAT TO CODE


Add recoverTool in agent.go. This example explicitly allows retry only for lookup_order because it
is a read. Return unresolved for an unknown write outcome.








server/agent.go


GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


// Only the named read-only tool can be retried without an external receipt.
func recoverTool(_ context.Context, request *gent.ToolRecoveryRequest) (
	*gent.ToolRecoveryResult, error,
) {
	status := gent.ToolRecoveryUnresolved
	if request.Name == "lookup_order" {
		status = gent.ToolRecoveryRetryAllowed
	}
	return &gent.ToolRecoveryResult{Status: status}, nil
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
ToolRecoveryUnresolved

    
Keep the unknown outcome visible to the model. Gent does not promise exactly-once external side
effects.

    2. 

  2. 
ToolRecoveryRetryAllowed

    
Use this only when retry is safe, such as this read-only tool or an operation protected by a stable
idempotency key.

    3. 

  3. 
ToolRecoveryCompleted

    
Return the complete saved result when an external receipt proves the operation finished.

    4. 

  4. 
ToolIdentityFromContext

    
Pass its stable ToolCallId to your external idempotency mechanism. A new attempt ID does not mean a
new logical operation.









RESULT


Completed steps are reused. Each unknown outcome has an explicit policy.







04 / FRESH WORKER STEP 04


Call Resume with fresh runtime bindings.



Rebuild the trace with trace.RestoreSequencer(saved, displayConfig(codecs)), then pass the new
recorder, codecs, observer, and recovery policy to Runner.Resume.



WHAT TO CODE


Add recover.go and call resumeSaved from the resume branch in API.start. Reuse the stored run ID. Do
not create a new Task or call Execute on a new context.








server/recover.go


GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


func resumeSaved(worker context.Context, saved gent.RunView, agent *react.Agent,
	writer gent.Recorder, seq *trace.Sequencer, codecs *gent.CodecRegistry,
) (*gent.ExecutionResult, error) {
	runner := executor.NewRunner(agent, executor.DefaultConfig())
	return runner.Resume(worker, saved, gent.RestoreBindings{
		Recorder: writer, Codecs: codecs,
		Observers:    []gent.RecordedEventObserver{seq},
		ToolRecovery: gent.ToolRecoveryFunc(recoverTool),
	})
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Preserved limits

    
Counters, original limits, and absolute deadlines survive restoration. Restarting the worker does
not extend the original deadline.

    2. 

  2. 
Runner.Resume

    
Configures the fresh agent, checks compatibility, restores state, and continues from the saved
control boundary.

    3. 

  3. 
Cursor after recovery

    
The next event follows RunView.LastAppliedEventNumber, even if the checkpoint cursor is older. The
frontend protocol stays the same.

    4. 

  4. 
Terminal run

    
A saved terminal run returns its recorded outcome without another model request or another accepted
answer event.









RESULT


The new worker continues the same saved run and publishes higher event numbers.







04 / FRESH WORKER STEP 05


Restart the process with the same database.



The example distinguishes a stopped worker from an intentional terminal run cancellation. Its
database keeps the last accepted progress and checkpoint.



WHAT TO CODE


Start an order lookup in the React page. Stop the Go process with Ctrl+C during the preview, restart
it with the same RUN_DB, then select Resume saved run.








server/http.go


GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


func (a *API) resumeRun(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.PathValue("id")
	if err := a.start(id, "", true); err != nil {
		writeError(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, map[string]string{"runId": id})
}




READ THE CODE
Line by line


  1. 
Keep the run ID

    
The React page keeps it in the URL. POST resume uses that ID and returns HTTP 409 if a worker is
already active.

    2. 

  2. 
Compatibility failures

    
Keep the original recovery version and declared configuration. Handle ErrIncompatibleCheckpoint
instead of forcing a restore.

    3. 

  3. 
Worker cancellation

    
Stopping the service interrupts the worker. ExecutionContext.CancelRun causes intentional terminal
cancellation.

    4. 

  4. 
Tests

    
The server tests reopen the database with fresh objects and resume both tool-ready and
tool-completed states. They also check terminal reuse.









RESULT


The React page catches up with the new worker through the same API.

All the pieces, ready to use.


These files are the source used by the example tests. Download the source
or copy a file into the matching path. The server and client archives include a README with
run commands.








main.go




GO
Source line numbers · Select a note to focus


package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/rickchristie/gent"
	"github.com/rickchristie/gent/models"
)

func env(name, fallback string) string {
	if value := os.Getenv(name); value != "" {
		return value
	}
	return fallback
}

func serve() error {
	worker, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	factory := func() gent.Model { return &DemoModel{Delay: 600 * time.Millisecond} }
	if key := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		name := os.Getenv("GENT_MODEL")
		if name == "" {
			return errors.New("set GENT_MODEL when using OPENAI_API_KEY")
		}
		factory = func() gent.Model { return models.NewOpenAI(key, name) }
	}
	codecs := gent.NewCodecRegistry()
	if err := newAgent(factory()).RegisterCodecs(codecs); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	store, err := openStore(env("RUN_DB", "runs.db"), codecs)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() {
		if err := store.db.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Printf("close database: %v", err)
		}
	}()
	api := &API{store: store, model: factory, worker: worker, running: map[string]*liveRun{}}
	listener, err := net.Listen("tcp", env("API_ADDR", "127.0.0.1:8080"))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	server := &http.Server{Handler: api.routes(env("UI_DIR", "../client/dist")),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}
	shutdown := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(shutdown)
		<-worker.Done()
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		if err := server.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
			log.Printf("HTTP shutdown: %v", err)
		}
	}()
	log.Printf("LISTEN http://%s", listener.Addr().String())
	err = server.Serve(listener)
	stop()
	<-shutdown
	api.wait.Wait()
	if errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
		return nil
	}
	return err
}

func main() {
	if err := serve(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

Line by line


  1. 
Own the worker context

    
Service shutdown cancels workers. A browser disconnect does not cancel them.

    2. 

  2. 
Keep the same database

    
Reopen this file after a restart to resume the same run and its event sequence.

    3. 

  3. 
Finish shutdown

    
Stop accepting HTTP work, then wait for the agent workers before closing the database.
